standardsRefs: Ready for Life v1, Grade 4 Unit 3: Kitchen Care and Food Safety
Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can practice cross-contamination basics. I will do one step at a time and check one result.
scenario: The learner is given six short written scenarios about food handling, some safe and some risky, such as using the same cutting board for raw chicken and then bread without washing it, or storing raw meat above ready-to-eat vegetables in a refrigerator.
materials: learner-local: paper or a notes app

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u03-l03-model-card. Watch one complete example.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u03-l03-guided-card. Do the coached move.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u03-l03-independent-card. Choose one complete route. Follow its steps.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u03-l03-evidence-record. Save one result and one reflection.

prompts.text: Which scenario was hardest to decide was safe or risky, and what extra information would have made the decision easier?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g4-u03-l03-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g4-u03-l03-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g4-u03-l03-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Risk identification accuracy: All six scenarios are sorted correctly, with the specific causing detail named for every scenario marked risky. | Fix specificity and germ-pathway reasoning: Each rewritten scenario names a specific fix and correctly explains what path from raw to ready-to-eat food that fix blocks. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g4-u03-l03-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner write two brand-new scenarios of their own, one safe and one risky, using a food and situation not covered in the original six, then trade with an adult or another learner in their household to sort.

resources.title: cross-contamination basics worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: The learner is given six short written scenarios about food handling, some safe and some risky, such as using the same cutting board for raw chicken and then bread without washing it, or storing raw meat above ready-to-eat vegetables in a refrigerator.

resources.title: cross-contamination basics coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The learner is given six short written scenarios about food handling, some safe and some risky, such as using the same cutting board for raw chicken and then bread without washing it, or storing raw meat above ready-to-eat vegetables in a refrigerator.
Coach direction: Before sorting anything, define the risk in your own words.
Learner prompt: In your own words, what does 'cross-contamination' mean, using the words 'raw' and 'germs' somewhere in your answer?
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: cross-contamination basics complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Read each of the six scenarios and sort it into 'safe' or 'risk,' marking which specific detail in the scenario made you decide.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I sorted all six scenarios into safe or risk.
Response 2 (t2-p2): For every scenario marked risk, I underlined or named the specific detail, such as a surface, utensil, or storage location, that caused it.
Response 3 (t2-p3): I did not mark a scenario risky just because it mentioned raw meat; I checked whether raw meat actually touched or dripped onto something ready-to-eat.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: cross-contamination basics minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Which scenario was hardest to decide was safe or risky, and what extra information would have made the decision easier?

Success checks: Risk identification accuracy: All six scenarios are sorted correctly, with the specific causing detail named for every scenario marked risky. | Fix specificity and germ-pathway reasoning: Each rewritten scenario names a specific fix and correctly explains what path from raw to ready-to-eat food that fix blocks.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: cross-contamination basics supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g4-u03-l03-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g4-u03-l03-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional cross-contamination basics condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Risk identification accuracy: All six scenarios are sorted correctly, with the specific causing detail named for every scenario marked risky. | Fix specificity and germ-pathway reasoning: Each rewritten scenario names a specific fix and correctly explains what path from raw to ready-to-eat food that fix blocks..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g4-u03-l03-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
